reason: The hand syringe and air tube look like the control connection needed to operate the distant jaws.

reason: The tube should link the hand control to the grabber’s output syringe.

choice.combine: Hand syringe with an air tube

reaction: I’m curious how well the enclosed air will move the jaws.

reaction: The springy response makes the air connection more interesting than a rigid linkage.
reason: The soft pads should help the jaws grip the pretend fruit gently.

reaction: The repeat test makes their purpose clear.

choice.with: Grabber with a secured air line

expectation: A squeeze will close the padded jaws around the fruit so it can be moved to the cup.

effect: The fruit test confirmed that the complete grabber can pick up and release an object from a distance, completing the goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the mechanism used for Kit’s game.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the air line with the block was most worthwhile: it showed how trapped air carries a push and why the response feels springy.

leastWorthwhile.text: Securing the tube and holder was practical but less interesting than testing the mechanism; the result added little explanation.

surprise.text: I was interested that the two plungers did not copy each other’s travel exactly because the trapped air compresses.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the parts and tests had clear purposes.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see what the fair does with these constructions; the hands-on tests and explanations made this mechanism feel worth exploring.
